utterances.text: In addition, Your Honour, we requested those too and those requests have been declined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, it's now 11.00. Is that a convenient moment for a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn. Today we'll take a 25-minute break. So 11.25, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, we'll go on. If possible, we would wish to complete this cross-examination today, from the point of view of the convenience of the witness, although he's apparently been informed that he may have to come back but, also, from the point of view of the trial itself, that we can contain this evidence, as it were, in one day. It's much easier to manage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'm very mindful of the Court's frustration with the apparently discussive nature of the questioning regarding general background witnesses, and I'll try to keep my questions harnessed directly to this witness's direct-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And if you could have in mind everybody else in the trial besides the questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: My deepest apologies to the people in the translation booth, and I'll try to keep it slow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. McLeod, I was intrigued by a comment that you made just a few minutes ago that you only had limited time available to do this report. Are you telling the Trial Chamber that there was a time limit placed upon you in preparing this report?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Because of that time limit, you didn't take the trouble to arrange a meeting with Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because I ran out of time in terms of the amount of time that I had been given. He was the last person that I was hoping to see and, unfortunately, I didn't get to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The time limit given by whom?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: The headquarters at ECMM had said that I should go down for about a week, do as much as I could and come back and write a report. So that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You came back and wrote the report without interviewing the person that you would now like to believe is the man calling the shots in Busovaca or Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What efforts did you make to try to arrange an appointment with Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: In practice, we didn't make any attempts at all to talk to him, although we had been intending to talk to him right at the end of the visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you pick up the telephone and call him?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you write him a letter asking to see him?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ask Ambassador Thebault to give him a call on the telephone to try to arrange an appointment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I haven't objected, but the question has been answered categorically "No," and if we want to move on, I think we can do so faster without asking the same question four or five times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I think we have the point that the witness did not meet Mr. Kordic, and I don't think we can take it much further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There's only one issue that I would like -- one question that I would like to ask, with the Court's permission, and that is whether he ever tried to arrange an appointment with Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me move on. Did you receive any written briefing materials from the European Community Monitoring Mission?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. As I've already described, I read all of their reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's permission, I'd just like to ask the witness whether he reviewed a report entitled "Introduction Brief for New ECMM Monitors," dated February 25th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have copies for everyone. I think there are enough here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D21/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just one question about this document, sir. If you could turn to page 6, there's a reference here to "A new formation of Muslim forces which accept only Islamic soldiers from Bosnia and abroad, assessed as being under 200 strong." That's paragraph 35. Did you receive, prior to your visit to the central Lasva Valley, any information regarding this formation? Is that a "No"?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sorry. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I've certainly heard of the 7th Muslim Brigade. I hadn't heard of them categorised as the Muslim forces army, which is what you're referring to in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of the MOS?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I wouldn't want to, at this point, try to remember exactly what "MOS" stood for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, before you began to meet with the people that you saw in the central Lasva Valley, did you take the time to take a look at the mutual agreements that had been signed between the HVO forces and the forces of the ABiH in February of 1993?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I probably would have seen them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask the usher to show you this document, which is -- all of these documents, by the way, Your Honour, have been provided to the Prosecution in advance.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D22/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If you would just take a look at this exhibit, Mr. McLeod, this consists of a series of orders jointly signed by Colonel Blaskic and Enver Hadzihasanovic, the commander of the 3rd Corps. Incidentally, the headquarters of the 3rd Corps was in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just one question about this document. Have you seen these orders before?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It's quite probable that I did, but looking at the distribution list on the front page, it's not clear it came to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The top distribution line says "HQ ECMM," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. For the chief of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just two pages from the back of this series of documents there's an order that relates to the filling in of trenches and bunkers, dated February the 13th, 1993. Were you aware that the HVO and the ABiH had agreed to fill in trenches and bunkers in February of the year in which you visited the central Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, because there had been a conflict in January, as a result of which the Busovaca joint commission was first established, and without actually -- I don't think I've seen these orders before, but clearly what it was doing was trying to stabilise the situation and go through a series of confidence-building measures, as they were called, which would include filling in trenches and bunkers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just another question relating to the Busovaca joint coordination commission. Did you ever see the charter of that particular organisation?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Possibly but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me show you another document that we would like to have marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D23/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This is a document that's apparently authored by Colonel Stewart in March of 1993, and if you take a look at the last page, it sets up the reporting structure, if you like, the chain of command for the joint coordination commission in Busovaca. The commanding officer, obviously, was from BritBat, and I take it that was Colonel Stewart; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I would assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The ECMM chairman, who would that be, sir?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I imagine that would be Jean-Pierre Thebault.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The other two individuals would be the commander of the 3rd Corps, General Enver Hadzihasanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the commander of the HVO, central command, and I believe that you have previously testified that was Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Then Colonel Blaskic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: By the way, you don't actually speak Croatian or you didn't at the time that you were in the central Lasva Valley, did you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not fluently, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you describe yourself as an expert in German?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have a degree in the language, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: An expert in German, though, the language?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: It depends what you're going to ask me. I think that probably the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the -- the second level of command, the command group, Busovaca joint commission? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure who the individuals would have been. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What effort did you make to find out about this joint body consisting of representatives of the British army, the organisation for which you worked, and the two opposing sides, the Croats and the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it would be fair to say that I was thoroughly aware of what was going on. I was completely aware of the fact that the joint commission was sitting and would see on a daily basis the results of what their actions were being reported up through the daily sit-reps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So the documents that you actually reviewed as you were coming up to speed to give yourself the background necessary to reach conclusions included a variety of reports generated by the joint coordination commission through the sit-reps and milinfosums?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So you were aware that in February and March of 1993, bodies existed upon which both Croats and Muslims sat trying to diffuse the tension, so to speak, presided over by British military forces and also the organisation for which you worked?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on May the 4th, you have testified that you arrived in Vitez; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you met with Colonel Stewart at that time?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Jean-Pierre Thebault was there as well?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Along with Thomas Osorio?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: An ECMM monitor; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was not an ECMM monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was -- I can't remember his exact title now. He was a civil rights investigator or an investigator of war crimes. I'm sure you know exactly what his precise title was. I can't remember precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There was another individual present in your entourage by the name of Payan Akhavan, I believe.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What was his job?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that he was a colleague of Thomas Osorio.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did those two gentleman arrive by happenstance or was that meeting prearranged, that they should be there as well you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I understand that they had arranged with Bob Stewart to be there. I think the happenstance, if you like, was that I was there at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How about the TV crew that was there? Was that a happenstance too or was that prearranged?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that that had been arranged between the TV crew and BritBat, but it was certainly nothing to do with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, the International Criminal Tribunal, wasn't that established in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have to admit that I have no idea when it was established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Sayers, you're not allowing time for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I have a note to myself to be slow here, Your Honour, and I am going to abide by that note.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On May the 5th, Mr. McLeod, do I take it that you spent your time collating and studying the reports that you had assembled?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Amongst the papers that you assembled to review, did you review an agreement dated April the 20th, 1993 following a meeting held in Zenica between General Morillon, Mr. Thebault, and actually signed by Sefer Halilovic of the ABiH, and General Petkovic, the HVO commander in chief? I'll give you a copy, if I may.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D24/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a few brief questions about this document. First, have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I probably have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you have any observations with respect to the first paragraph of this agreement, that the BiH army and HVO are both legal military forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and are treated equally?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you're asking me to comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear, during your brief sojourn in the Lasva Valley, contentions to the effect that somehow the HVO was not a legal entity or organisation?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you understand that there was a division in the HVO between the civil side and the military side?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I was aware, the HVO was a military organisation and the HDZ would be the political organisation, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Okay. Turning to the next day that you spent in the central Lasva Valley, May the 6th, I take it that your process of assimilating the written information continued during that day. You didn't actually meet with anybody during that day?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Turning to May the 7th, I understand that you had four meetings on that day: The first with the mayor of Zenica, a man by the name of Besim Spahic; the second with a Catholic priest in Zenica, Father Stjepan; the third with the head of the International Red Cross Committee in Zenica; and then the fourth with the commander of the 3rd Corps in Zenica, General Hadzihasanovic; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the interpreter that you used during those meetings, sir?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In your meeting with Mr. Spahic, the mayor, there was also a press officer present, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Spahic told you that the problems, to use the word that you use in annex A of your report, the problems had started on April the 16th?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know anything about a situation in which 13 Croats had been killed in the village of Dusina in January of 1993 and 30 people arrested as well?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sure that I was aware of it, but at this stage, I'm not sure I have a note which would suggest exactly to prove that I was aware of it, but I probably was aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just going over your meeting with Mr. Spahic, he acknowledged to you that Croat houses had been burned, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Croats had been evicted from their residences?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Croats had been arrested en masse; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Allowing the pause before I answer. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He gave you some documents that you actually appended --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Sayers, you asked the witness to confirm that Croats had been arrested en masse, arrested, evicted from their homes and so on. Could we know from the witness or from you yourself at what time and in what locality that happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Judge Bennouna. I'll address that question immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Amongst the briefing materials that you assembled for yourself, did you actually take a look at a report, a special report on Croats in Zenica, dated April 20 to 21, 1993? I have a copy of that for the Court, and for you and the other side, and co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D25/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: A few questions, Mr. McLeod, on this document. Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Since I'm on the distribution list, I'm sure I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This was one of the documents that you had available to you as you were conducting your inquiries?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You had been informed that about 200 Croats -- about 200 Croats had been arrested, half military, half civilian, as you can see, and about 30 showed signs of brutality; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There's a reference in the first paragraph, right at the end of it, to possible detention centres, one of which is the music -- it says "cool" but it should be school; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You had heard about the music school before, had you not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You never actually visited the music school, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That was a detention facility of a special force, a special unit of the ABiH, the 7th Muslim Brigade, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: In light of everything else that I heard then, yes, I think that it probably was. At the time, I'm not sure that it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You had doubt in your mind at this time what it was?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I understood that there was a detention centre in the music school. I'm not sure at this time that I knew who was controlling it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The second paragraph goes on to detail the houses that had been burned, Croat houses, that is, in numerous villages, and I won't recite them because the document says what it says. These houses had all been burned actually shortly before or in the weeks before the date that this report was actually prepared; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's clear when actually it happened and, therefore, I'm not sure if it would be in the weeks before or just the days before, but certainly they had been burnt, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Recently, you would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You knew that HVO soldiers who wanted to return to their villages that had been burned down, plundered, and so forth were free to do so, provided they turned in their weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was my understanding of what was -- I don't know if it was being agreed, but that was what people were trying to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you gave some testimony about 2.000 or so Croats who had been turned out of Zenica, and you gave or at least you reported in your report that this was an elaborate ruse on the part of the Croats, somehow to come up with an excuse for the attack on Vitez. Do you remember that in your report?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Which of these 2.000 Croats did you talk to to verify that, any of them?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I spoke to the -- as you're aware, I spoke to the religious Catholic priests who were there in Zenica, and they were some of the people who gave me the impression which I formed which I then wrote down in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But to get back to my question, you didn't speak to a single one of these refugees, did you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, there's another fellow by the name of Sakic who's referred to in your report as the president of the HDZ in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sakic. Take a look at annex A of your report, sir, page A1.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm with you, yes. Yes, I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, this was Mr. Dominik Sakic, right, or did you know?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think what I'm doing here is simply writing down what I was being told. I'm not sure that I actually checked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. So you just recorded what you had been told by the Muslim mayor of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You didn't ask to see, I take it, Mr. Sakic, who was the political leader of the Croatian Community in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Even though you knew his name?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. On the second page, page A2, you record here that mister -- on the second page, you record that supposedly Mr. Sakic had asked the mayor, Mr. Spahic, to arrest him?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's what I was told. I have no idea whether it was true or not. I was simply writing down what I was being told.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Mayor Spahic told you about Croat houses being set on fire, did he not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And various villages, a variety of them, and they are all listed in your report; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The next meeting that you had was with Father Stjepan; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That is in exhibit or appendix B to your report or annex B; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I could just ask you to turn back to page A1-1, I just have a couple of questions about this document. This was one of the documents you were given by Mayor Spahic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, paragraph 3 refers to a Mr. Zivko Totic. Did you know that Mr. Zivko Totic was a local HVO military commander who had been kidnapped on April the 15th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Sayers. Which paragraph, which page? I am a little bit lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I hope we all have the same documents, but as I understand it, Judge Bennouna --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Annex B?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's annex A1-1, and I'm actually referring to the third paragraph down. It's in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, Your Honour: "Civil police authorities have to do their best to investigate the crimes committed within the last three days to find out who did these crimes and to enable Mr. Zivko Totic to be released." Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Page A1-1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The one at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The one I have on the bottom of my version, Your Honour, is 020186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will have to start at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Who is Mr. Totic?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know who Mr. Totic is, but from the description that you just gave, then I assume that he is one of the HVO officers who were kidnapped as reported by, I think, probably ECMM on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that his three bodyguards that evening, April the 15th, 1993, had been assassinated in a hail of gunfire in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that these gentleman had been -- or Mr. Totic was apprehended by supposedly Mujahedin of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't think I was aware of that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever see a copy of the ransom note or the exchange note, the demand note, that had been provided to the ECMM by the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Possibly, but if you would show me, I would be happy to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'd be happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D26/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just one brief question on this, Mr. McLeod. Have you ever seen this handwritten note before?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Possibly, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You actually heard, though, that a request had been made by the Mujahedin to exchange Mr. Totic and others for foreign prisoners being held by the HVO, all from different countries; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could we go to exhibit or annex B to your report that chronicles your meeting with Father Stjepan? Now, just a few things on this, Mr. McLeod. One of the first things that Father Stjepan complained about to you was that 21 people were missing and not actually in gaol. He believed that they were in the music school or with the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What effort did you undertake to find out what this 7th Muslim Brigade actually was?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: As you will see two interviews further down with Jean-Pierre Thebault, we went to speak to Mr. Hadzihasanovic, who was the commander of the 3rd Brigade, and Jean-Pierre made a fairly strong demarche to him, suggesting that what we had just been told should be investigated and that there should be the possibility of having access to these detention centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. What efforts did you make to find out what this 7th Muslim Brigade was, other than having a talk with General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: We pressed both Hadzihasanovic and then also, I don't know if it's Dugalic, who was one of his deputy commanders, to provide us access to the facilities, because as far as we could hear, people were being detained and we wanted to try to get access to both sides to see what condition they were in and to secure their release.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That would have been fairly important to determine in your investigations and inquiries, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that never happened, did it?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, as you're aware, we got access to Kaonik prison --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. McLeod, that wasn't my question. My question was: Did you ever get access to the music school detention facility or find out -- get access to the headquarters of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I apologise. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Father Stjepan complained to you about a massacre of Croats in the village of Miletici, did he not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: People had had their hands tied behind their back, were shot in the head, and were then burned; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you knew about that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I don't believe that appears anywhere in your one-page report, does it, the report on inter-ethnic violence in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Father Stjepan also told you about something called the MOS from the town of Zepce to the north, and these people were more brutal than local people, he told you; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What effort did you find out -- what effort did you undertake to determine the identity of these individuals, the MOS?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You told Judge Riad, two years ago in the Blaskic case, that you didn't know what this entity even was; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Father Stjepan told you that 250 to 260 Croat families had been expelled from their houses; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There's no mention of that in your report either, is there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That 40 houses had been burned and plundered; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All belonging to Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He complained about discrimination against Croats, did he not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You had no reason to disbelieve the complaints being made to you by this Catholic priest, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: None at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: None at all. There's no reference to that anywhere in your report, is there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: There's no reference to that on the front page of the report, but the full details of what he was saying were contained within the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, I believe Father Stjepan told you that the MOS consisted of Mujahedin and foreigners who were the most extreme group in Bosnia-Herzegovina and that they were totally out of control; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I apologise if it actually says it in my report. I've already said -- yes, on page B2, halfway down, you can see him saying that MOS are not foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right, sir. You had no reason to disbelieve that, did you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yet again, what I'm doing is just writing down what people are saying to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. But you made -- well, I think you've already answered that question. The next thing that you did is go to see Jean-Luc Novarraz (phoen) from the ICRC later on May the 7th, and that's -- you reproduced a version of what occurred at that meeting in annex C to your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were told that the ICRC only had access to the main prison in Zenica but not to the Ministry of the Interior, the MUP prison, or to the music school; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You put a little comment up at the top here saying: "Since access to prisons was a major concern," you wanted to make sure that what was being done was coordinating it with the ICRC; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, you were given free access to the Kaonik facility by the Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's the only gaol you visited in your brief tour through the Lasva Valley; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You never visited the gaol in Zenica, did you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Despite knowing that there were about 280 prisoners there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I wonder if this is fair to the witness, because the sentence goes on, if you read it: "I said that we were working on access for us and Father Stjepan within the context of the political pressure we were applying." So the witness makes it clear in the document that they were attempting to gain access. I don't know that this is a fair question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. That may be, Judge May. So let me just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The point being that you didn't actually visit any prisons in Zenica, either open or closed; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And made no effort to do that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would not agree that I made no effort to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: What effort did you make to do that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think if you look at the notes of my meetings with Dugalic, that we had said that we wanted access and this had been tentatively agreed as being possible, and then in practice, because of the demarche I made to Dugalic, he arranged for the nine Croat prisoners from the main prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Suffice it to say you were never given any access to the Muslim prison facilities in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you speak up, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Suffice it to say you were never given any access to the Muslim prison facilities in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next meeting that you had was with General Hadzihasanovic, and that is reported at annex D of your report?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Jean-Pierre Thebault was with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: It would be more accurate to say that I was with him because he was leading the meeting but, yes, we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He was doing all the talking and you were just listening?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And writing?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. He was actually the head of the ECMM reporting cell in Zenica, was he not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You raised the subject of access to prisoners with the General; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the subject of hostages?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Those were Croat hostages; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would infer it from the note. I can't remember the conversation in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Was there any discussion of Mr. Totic who was being detained by Mujahedins at that time?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this stage, I can't remember exactly. That was probably the subject of discussion, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The General told you that he had no knowledge of the music school or the Ministry of the Interior prison, did he not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think he contradicted himself, because as you can see, he claimed to have no knowledge but he then said that access would not be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But he told you that it was best to go slowly, right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And because the 7th Muslim Brigade was not under control?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There are many elements, he said, who are not controlled. That's not clear to me from your notes. Were you referring to other elements than the 7th Muslim Brigade or merely to the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly who he was referring to. I think he was simply saying there were many elements that are not controlled. He could have been referring to anything. At this point I can't be more precise, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you able to determine, Mr. McLeod, where the 7th Muslim Brigade fit within the chain of command of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I understood that they were part of 3 Corps, although what was being suggested in this meeting was that their connection was fairly tentative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I see. All right. Well, let's turn to the next day, May the 8th.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: You conducted a series of investigations on May the 8th. The first with Father Bozo in the village of Cajdras, right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's a few kilometres southwest of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He repeated the same story that you had been told before and had read in ECMM documents that a large number of Croat houses had been burned, large numbers of Croats had been evicted from their houses and chased out of the territory, and that their houses had been plundered and robbed; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And burned down?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Once again, though there's no mention of that in your report, is there, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Referring to the report is confusing. This is the report that we're looking at. I take it you mean the summary?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Without belabouring that report, Mr. McLeod, this gentleman, Father Bozo, also brought up the 7th Muslim Brigade and the music school detention facility, did he not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And he repeated the concerns that he had about the 21 missing people who were detained there; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Father Bozo also told you about the MOS making nightly arrests at various villages, slaughtering animals, and performing various other forms of criminal activity, did he not? It's on page E2 in the middle or just above the middle.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The Court can read the tale of burnings for itself. I won't belabour that point. Did you ever become aware of any facts that would suggest that the statistical information or the factual information contained in this report of mass burnings and plunder and so forth, killings, was inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Father Bozo actually gave you a letter that he had sent to the commander of the 3rd Corps, and I believe that that is attached to your -- to the overall document.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think if we call it my report, then that's useful. It's appendix 1 to annex E of my report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On the first page, there's a reference to the 7th Muslim Brigade. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And a general complaint about discrimination against Croats in the Zenica area. In fact, that's in bold letters. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You weren't aware of any facts that led you to believe that there, in fact, was not discrimination against Croats in the Zenica area, were you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next meeting that you had was later that day with Ivan Santic, the mayor of Vitez, and Pero Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Santic was a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this stage, I can't remember whether he was a member of the HVO or a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How about Mr. Skopljak? Was he a member of the HVO or not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think he was a member of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever make an attempt to see Dr. Mujezinovic, the Muslim president of the Vitez war presidency?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you know that he was actually in Vitez as you were travelling around visiting Mr. Santic and Mr. Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I became aware of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But you made no attempt to see him?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, in your notes, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In your notes, the notes that you took of your meeting with Mr. Santic and Mr. Skopljak, page 35, specifically, I'd like to refer you to -- there's a reference to Dusina. I don't know if the Trial Chamber actually has these notes. It might make sense to put them on the ELMO. You see the word "Dusina" shortly down from the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do I take it that Mr. Santic and Mr. Skopljak were discussing the subject of the village of Dusina with you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just trying to find the same place in my typed note. Can you assist me? Do you have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think you will actually find it in there, but -- I can't actually find it in here, Mr. McLeod, but let me just ask you --

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm trying to find the paragraph above it so I can place it in context, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think it's page F2 right at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You agree that there's no discussion in your notes of the village of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. On the basis that I've written the word "Dusina," but there's nothing else in my written note to help me, so when I was typing it up, I've missed it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You recognise Dusina as the village that I alluded to earlier, the village that had been the subject of a massacre of about 13 Croat civilians in January?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the purpose of the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I was just inquiring why that subject had been omitted from the typed version of this report, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think the answer is very simple. As you can see in the original note, I've simply written the word "Dusina," and when I was typing it up, because I had nothing other than "Dusina" to prompt my memory, I've taken the typed record of the meeting from the paragraph above here (indicating) and continued there because there was nothing other than just the word "Dusina" to remind me what we've just been talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just one other question regarding your report, page F2. You were told that the Mujahedin from Zenica and the 7th Muslim Brigade had been seen coming down a hill from the village of Vjetrenice; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether that was true?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Again, I have no idea whether it was true or not. I was simply writing the note as he was speaking or as the translator was interpreting for me, and that's what I captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The next visit that you paid on May the 8th was to Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know the system of ranks in the HVO at all?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not with detail, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the term "pukovnik" means lieutenant colonel or whether it means colonel?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you ever heard the term "potpukovnik"?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I may have done but I certainly can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. As I understand it, you conclude, sir, that the story you were told by Mr. Santic, Mr. Skopljak, and Colonel Blaskic that there was an attack by Muslim forces on the town of Vitez on the 16th of April, 1993 was, to use your words, incredible?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a document entitled "Final Report of the United Nations Commission of Experts Established Pursuant to Security Council Resolution 780 of 1992," and specifically annex 3A regarding special forces, the report prepared under the direction of M. Cherif Bassiouni?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's the relevance of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The relevance is, Your Honour, that this report concludes: "It was reported that a unit of the Mujahedin, the guerilla, participated in the 16th of April, 1993 attack on Vitez and attempted to exchange ten HVO hostages for foreign prisoners held in HVO prisons."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the date of that report?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The date of the report is December the 28th, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can call evidence about it if you want. Do you know anything about this report, Mr. McLeod?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Did you know that your report, your own report, was cited as one of the sources in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He doesn't know anything about the report, so he can't answer that. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Going back to your meeting with Colonel Blaskic, you saw him as the chief military figure on behalf of the HVO in Central Bosnia, did you not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The meeting was relaxed and business-like, as you've recorded?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's how I characterised it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You considered him straightforward and honest?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. If I can say more than just "Yes" or "No" to help you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No. You can help the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. You can help us. You can conclude your answer. What is it?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were having a conversation as to -- as I already said, one serving soldier, one retired soldier, and his description of the military situation and the events which had taken place after the 16th was very straightforward and matched -- was almost word for word the same description that I had had from BritBat who was sitting observing exactly the same events. So from that point of view, it was relaxed, straightforward. He had no difficulty showing me on the map the various things which he wanted to point out to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You found his assessment of the military situation to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There's no question in your mind that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was fully capable of launching an attack in Central Bosnia on the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and to expand on that again, if it's useful, patently they were capable of doing that because they did mount an attack after the 16th. The debate can be whether it was an attack or counter-attack but, de facto, they did amount an attack which was only prevented from, as far as I could see, achieving what Colonel Blaskic thought was the outcome by the intervention of the International Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Is it your impression or opinion that the village of Ahmici was completely undefended?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would imagine that the village of Ahmici was defended up to a point, but whatever defence there was not particularly successful, I think would be how I would characterise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Were you told that it was undefended at any time?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: None of the British military figures involved told you that this was a completely defenceless, undefended village?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember whether anybody actually described it as either defended or undefended.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Were you ever shown a statement by a gentleman by the name of Fuad Berbic, which has been entered into evidence in this case as Exhibit D13/2?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In coming up with your opinion as to who it was who was responsible for Ahmici, would it have helped you to review reports from people who actually were there during the attack or the hostilities?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sure it would have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I got as close as reports of what they had said as opposed to actually talking to any individuals who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So you never actually spoke face to face with anybody who was actually in the village during the evening or morning of April the 15th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So everything that you know is second-hand or thirdhand?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The final meeting that you had, I believe, on May 8th was the deputy commander of the Kruscica Brigade of the ABiH, another military commander by the name of Huke Halilovic; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's exhibit H or annex H. Kruscica is about one kilometre south of Vitez, is it not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, south or southwest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the deputy commander of the Kruscica Brigade who you met on May the 8th?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure I actually wrote his name down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Once again, these gentlemen told you a familiar story, that Croat houses had been burned but by Muslim extremists who were not under military control, to use their words; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on May the 9th, you met with the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, and this is annex I now, I believe, Mr. Ramiz Dugalic --

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: -- to begin the day. Was there anybody else present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was Eric Friis-Pedersen, our interpreter. I can't remember whether there was anybody else on his side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did they suggest to you any names of people that you might want to see? Don't mention the name, please.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, I would just like to have a document shown to Mr. McLeod relating to a witness who has testified in private session and just ask him if he recognises this name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Would you respond for the record, please, Mr. McLeod?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly. I don't recognise the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Return it to counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we see it, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let Mr. Scott see it first, please, and then return it to counsel. Yes, Mr. Sayers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'm trying to move along, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Court will know from the days and weeks of trial that we have not objected very much to cross-examination, but this has been a continual process of going through the notes which the information is, in fact, included in the report. This is the report, not simply page 1, and then repeatedly they're indicating, "Well, is it in the summary or not?" There's a fair amount of cross-examination I think we've allowed, but we're not halfway through the document or halfway through the notes, and if we're going to do this page by page, we're going to be here for a very long time. I think if he can make the point straight out to the witness, we'll get there a lot quicker, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I agree, but you cannot prevent him highlighting, if he wants to, all the evidence which is favourable to his side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Then, no doubt, we can rule, if necessary, that you may go through all the items and highlight those favourable to your side. Whether we find it helpful, that is another matter. Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Could you turn to page 57 of your handwritten notes and just put those on the ELMO? Unfortunately, they don't really read very well. There are two names at the top of your May the 5th or May the 9th, rather, 1993 note regarding the meeting with the imam of Busovaca, and the two names are Ramiz Dugalic, 3rd Corps something. Could you just tell us what that says, please?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: 3rd Corps deputy commander for security, for SIS or security.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The second name is -- could you just read that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's Jasmin, 7th Muslim Brigade military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you meet with that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know why his name is down there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this stage, I have no idea. No. Certainly, they were not present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The second meeting that you had on May the 9th was with Major Brian Watters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You didn't make any notes of that meeting, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. We were running through the BritBat reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You had a long conversation with him though, I take it?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did he tell you that Dzemo Merdan had ordered the blockade, the ABiH blockade to be erected at the village of Ahmici on October the 20th, 1992, just a few months before?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You met with Colonel Watters alone, did you not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this stage, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Turning to your meeting with the imam, he told you that he had a pass signed by three separate people, dated May the 1st, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The first of those names is Dusko Grubesic, the commander of the HVO brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think you previously acknowledged that you made no effort to contact that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The next person was Zoran Maric, who was the president of the HVO in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You made no effort to contact him?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Then the third person was Mr. Dario Kordic of the HDZ. Do you remember the subject of the statement "Kordic seems to be the man calling the shots" coming up very extensively in the Blaskic case?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly because there, amongst other things, was perhaps a mistranslation into one of the versions, so we went round the houses several times on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In that case, you testified that you have no idea what the phrase means, that you couldn't remember; right? That was on January the 20th, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which phrase?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That Kordic would be the man calling the shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you remember that subject coming up when you were giving that testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you don't remember, say so, Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, sir, I have the transcript of that testimony so that I can remind myself of exactly what was said. I do remember the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that's what you said; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I remind myself of what I said?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we have a page, please, Counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes. It's page 6455 to 6456 of the Blaskic transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You said "Four and a half years on --"

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think refreshing my memory, the issue where you're asking me whether I have no idea of whether it exists or not, that's me referring to whether that idiom exists within the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were actually asked, just a few pages earlier on page 6376, "Is that a quote from the imam?" and your response was, "No."

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, because it is -- it's difficult now, six years later, to remember the precise flow of the conversation. I have shown you my contemporaneous note. It's quite clear that that's what I wrote at the time. I believe that that was my summary of where we had got to as opposed to what the imam himself actually said, but I apologise for the fact that at this stage I can't just produce the taperecorder and play the recording back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Your next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Sayers, may I remind you that that was an answer that was already given to the question I asked before to the witness about this very same phrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The next meeting that you had was with several police officers in Busovaca; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were told that a military policeman had been shot the night before by a sniper in Busovaca; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that there were problems with the MOS in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You were meeting with these people, I take it, sir, because you wanted to find out who was actually in control of the situation in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in practice this was a slightly impromptu meeting because as was noted on the end of the previous annex, as I was concluding my meeting with the imam, the police arrived at his house. They wanted to talk to me there, and I suggested that perhaps I should accompany them back to the police station and we then had this meeting. So it was not previously arranged, but I was quite content to talk to them because it gave me that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Are you sure that the people that came to the imam's door are the same people that you interviewed with?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were police -- Croatian police came to the house, and I then accompanied them back and had this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Haven't you previously stated that you're not sure whether the three people that you met with are the three people that came to the imam's door?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: At this stage I simply can't remember the faces, but I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's try to speed up a little bit here. Going to May the 10th, you had a second meeting with the mayor of Zenica, and that's annex M?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There's only one point I'd like to make there. You made a reference there to a letter that had supposedly been sent by Mr. Boban, that is reported to have outlined a case against Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you attach that or did you have a copy of it with you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think I may well have had a copy with me at the time that I was talking to him. I didn't have a copy -- I think it was Jean-Pierre Thebault's copy. I didn't have a copy when I was making my report or I would have attached it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me show you a document and ask you if this is the copy to which you were referring.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D27/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This is a joint statement signed by Mate Boban and Alija Izetbegovic, dated April the 25th, 1993 and communicated to the United Nations Security Council a day later. Is this the document to which you were referring?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you actually have in your files a copy of the document to which you were referring which contain the statements supposedly made by Mr. Boban?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. As I already said, if I did, then I would have attached it at the back of the report, but when I was creating the report, I didn't have a copy anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, you met with Mr. Aleksovski, I believe, shortly after a meeting with representatives of the Centre for Human Rights?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The purpose of the Centre for Human Rights was to uncover crimes committed by the HVO in the last year; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I think they were trying to investigate various things that had happened. I'm not sure that I actually saw a copy of their charter, if they had such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If you just take a look at annex N1, that's "N" for "November," of your report, right at the bottom of the page there?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. This centre was not aimed in any way at trying to uncover crimes that Muslims had committed against Croats, was it? It was just a one-way Tribunal, if you like?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I was not entirely impressed by some of the information which they were giving me, but again, what I was doing was just writing down exactly what they said and copying any documents which they gave me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, during your meeting with Mr. Aleksovski, and I think that you have summarised that at annex O?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You saw no signs of any physical injury demonstrated on any of the detainees at that facility, did you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There were about 79 Muslim detainees at the time that you were there; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There was no attempt to hide the conditions under which they were interned or to prevent you from speaking with anyone that you wanted to speak to?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There were also about 30 Croats gaoled at that time in the military gaol; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that there were 30 of them. I saw two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. How long did you spend at this facility?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think in my notes or certainly in my previous testimony, it was between an hour and two hours. I didn't make a note of the time exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were accompanied by Ambassador Thebault?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He was doing most of the talking; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Once again, two familiar themes appear in the notes. Mr. Aleksovski complained about the activities of the 7th Muslim Brigade, did he not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He also mentioned the incident at Dusina to you. If you take a look at page 0-4, I think you'll find a reference there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's 0-4, Your Honours, and the passage is just below the middle of the page. It says: "For example, our people from Kacuni were all expelled and then they burned the whole village."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The first case happened in Dusina; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Were you ever informed by way of milinfosum or otherwise that the heart of the HVO commander of the forces defending Dusina had been cut out from his body after he had been killed?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, we have the reference here to what Mr. Aleksovski told me. I can't honestly remember reading it in any of the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you weren't prohibited from speaking to anybody that you wanted; I think you've stated that. The people that you did speak to told you that they had been well-treated, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: They did say that. I'm not sure that I necessarily believed, as I think I've said in previous testimony, that what they were saying was not slightly scripted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, that's what they told you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: They looked well-fed; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure that they looked well-fed. They didn't look as if they were starving.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: There's a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The ablutions were basic but clean?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And Mr. Aleksovski's two principal complaints were that he had a lack of food generally; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that he didn't have enough security forces in his own gaol basically to take care of the people that were in there; right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Okay. I think that brings us, with one exception, down to the people that you saw during your visit. I believe that you went back to see Ramiz Dugalic again on May the 11th?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that he was trying to persuade you that it was actually the HVO that was responsible for the attacks and the hostilities in Ahmici and Vitez in the middle of April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You did not do any interviews on May the 12th?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have about, I would say, 20 minutes more. This would be a convenient point to break because I know Mr. Mikulicic will want some cross-examination. I apologise for having to bring this gentleman back. This might be a convenient point to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, is it right that you're going to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, Your Honour. I should also like to ask several questions, but I do not think I should be needing more than one hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, in that case, this would be a convenient time. Mr. McLeod, I'm afraid I shall have to ask you to come back. I hope that it's possible to find a convenient time as soon as possible to complete your evidence. Meanwhile, would you remember what I said earlier in relation to speaking to anybody about your evidence? Don't do so, apart from making arrangements with the Prosecution about returning. Now, I'll be reminded when we're going to sit again. The matters to be dealt with, as far as evidence is concerned, will be heard next on Monday, the 31st of May, at 3.00 p.m. We will adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a tad confused. That's relative to the search and seizure issues on the 31st?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If that's what we ordered, that's what it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's our understanding as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
